- 59:7 (the allocation of what was returned) is not drafted because it is legal in kind.

## How to review

## 1. Driven from their homes  (`#driven-from-their-homes`)

Cited ayat: 59:2-5

> **59:2** هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَخْرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمْ لِأَوَّلِ ٱلْحَشْرِ مَا ظَنَنتُمْ أَن يَخْرُجُوا۟ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا۟ وَقَذَفَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعْبَ يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَيْدِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَٱعْتَبِرُوا۟ يَٰٓأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ
>
> **59:3** وَلَوْلَآ أَن كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْجَلَآءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمْ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَلَهُمْ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ عَذَابُ ٱلنَّارِ
>
> **59:4** ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ شَآقُّوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَمَن يُشَآقِّ ٱللَّهَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ
>
> **59:5** مَا قَطَعْتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوْ تَرَكْتُمُوهَا قَآئِمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيُخْزِىَ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (59:2): God drove out those of the People of the Book who disbelieved from their homes at the first gathering; the believers did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from God; but God came upon them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; take a lesson, you who have sight.

**c2** (59:3): Had God not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world; and in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.

**c3** (59:4): That was because they opposed God and His Messenger; whoever opposes God, God is severe in punishment.

**c4** (59:5): Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.

### One-minute summary

God drove out those of the People of the Book who disbelieved from their homes, and they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers [c1]. The ayat say that they opposed God and His Messenger, and that God had decreed exile for them [c2][c3].

### Complete story

God drove out those of the People of the Book who disbelieved from their homes at the first gathering [c1]. The believers did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from God; but God came upon them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts [c1]. They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; take a lesson, you who have sight [c1].

Had God not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world; and in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire [c2]. That was because they opposed God and His Messenger; whoever opposes God, God is severe in punishment [c3].

Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient [c4].

### Deep study

The ayat give the believers' view and the expelled party's view of the same event: the believers did not expect them to leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them [c1]. The expulsion is called exile, a thing decreed, and the alternative is stated as punishment in this world [c2]. The ayah on the palm trees says that what was cut or left standing was by God's leave [c4].

### Kids mode

A group of the People of the Book had to leave their homes, though they thought their fortresses would protect them [c1]. God said that He had decreed exile for them [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat say that fortresses did not protect them from God, and ask the hearer to take a lesson [c1]. Another is that the ayat give the reason as opposing God and His Messenger [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the party of the People of the Book was by name, where they lived, when they left, or where they went; the ayat describe them and do not name them.
- Not established: what the first gathering was, or how it relates to a later gathering.
- Not established: which palm trees these were, or how many.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the party, the place and the date. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

## 2. What was returned, and the prayer of those who came after  (`#what-was-returned-and-the-prayer`)

Cited ayat: 59:6, 59:10

> **59:6** وَمَآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنْهُمْ فَمَآ أَوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خَيْلٍ وَلَا رِكَابٍ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُۥ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

> **59:10** وَٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَٰنِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِٱلْإِيمَٰنِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ فِى قُلُوبِنَا غِلًّا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (59:6): What God returned to His Messenger from them was not something for which the believers had urged horse or camel, but God gives His messengers power over whom He wills; God has power over all things.

**c2** (59:10): Those who came after them say: our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place any resentment in our hearts toward those who believe; our Lord, You are kind and merciful.

### One-minute summary

The ayat say that what God returned to His Messenger from them was not gained by the believers urging horse or camel, but that God gives His messengers power over whom He wills [c1]. They record the prayer of those who came after: to forgive them and their brothers who preceded them in faith and to place no resentment in their hearts [c2].

### Complete story

What God returned to His Messenger from them was not something for which the believers had urged horse or camel, but God gives His messengers power over whom He wills; God has power over all things [c1].

Those who came after them say: our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place any resentment in our hearts toward those who believe; our Lord, You are kind and merciful [c2].

### Deep study

The first ayah explains how the matter came about by saying that it was not by urging horse or camel [c1]. The next ayah is a prayer spoken by later believers for those who preceded them in faith [c2].

### Kids mode

The ayat say that God gives His messengers power over whom He wills [c1]. Later believers pray for their brothers who came before them and ask for no resentment in their hearts [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the prayer asks for forgiveness for those who came earlier and for freedom from resentment [c2]. Another is that the first ayah ties the matter to God's power over all things [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what exactly was returned, how it was used, or who received it; the allocation (59:7) is legal in kind and is not drafted here.
- Not established: who those who came after are by name, or when they came.
- Not established: how this prayer relates in time to the expulsion.
- The ayat do not say how much was returned.

## 3. The hypocrites' promise  (`#the-hypocrites-promise`)

Cited ayat: 59:11-14

> **59:11** أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ نَافَقُوا۟ يَقُولُونَ لِإِخْوَٰنِهِمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَئِنْ أُخْرِجْتُمْ لَنَخْرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمْ وَلَا نُطِيعُ فِيكُمْ أَحَدًا أَبَدًا وَإِن قُوتِلْتُمْ لَنَنصُرَنَّكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
>
> **59:12** لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُوا۟ لَا يَخْرُجُونَ مَعَهُمْ وَلَئِن قُوتِلُوا۟ لَا يَنصُرُونَهُمْ وَلَئِن نَّصَرُوهُمْ لَيُوَلُّنَّ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
>
> **59:13** لَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ رَهْبَةً فِى صُدُورِهِم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَّا يَفْقَهُونَ
>
> **59:14** لَا يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمْ جَمِيعًا إِلَّا فِى قُرًى مُّحَصَّنَةٍ أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ جُدُرٍۭ بَأْسُهُم بَيْنَهُمْ شَدِيدٌ تَحْسَبُهُمْ جَمِيعًا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّىٰ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَّا يَعْقِلُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (59:11): Those who showed hypocrisy said to their brothers among the People of the Book who disbelieved: if you are driven out, we will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you; and if you are fought, we will help you; God testifies that they are liars.

**c2** (59:12): If they were driven out, they would not go out with them; if they were fought, they would not help them; and if they helped them, they would turn their backs and then not be helped.

**c3** (59:13): They have more fear of the believers in their hearts than of God, because they are a people who do not understand.

**c4** (59:14): They will not fight the believers all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls; their violence among themselves is severe; you think them united while their hearts are divided, because they are a people who do not reason.

### One-minute summary

The ayat say that the hypocrites promised their brothers among the People of the Book to go out with them and to help them, and that God testifies they are liars [c1]. They say that if driven out they would not go out with them, and that if fought they would not help them [c2].

### Complete story

Those who showed hypocrisy said to their brothers among the People of the Book who disbelieved: if you are driven out, we will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you; and if you are fought, we will help you; God testifies that they are liars [c1].

If they were driven out, they would not go out with them; if they were fought, they would not help them; and if they helped them, they would turn their backs and then not be helped [c2]. They have more fear of the believers in their hearts than of God, because they are a people who do not understand [c3].

They will not fight the believers all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls; their violence among themselves is severe; you think them united while their hearts are divided, because they are a people who do not reason [c4].

### Deep study

The ayat quote the hypocrites' promise and then answer it with God's testimony that they are liars [c1]. They give the answer in a series of conditions: driven out, fought, and helping [c2]. The last ayat explain the failure by what is in the hearts: fear of the believers more than of God, and divided hearts [c3][c4].

### Kids mode

Some people who were not sincere promised their friends to help them, but God said they were not telling the truth [c1]. The ayat say that their hearts were divided [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show a promise made without sincerity and what happens to it [c1][c2]. Another is that the ayat find the cause in hearts that are divided and do not understand [c3][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the hypocrites were by name, or when and to whom they spoke; the ayat describe them and do not name them.
- Not established: whether the promise was ever put to the test, beyond what the ayat say would happen.
- Not established: where the fortified towns were.
- The ayat do not say how many they were.

## 4. Like those before, and like Satan  (`#like-those-before-and-like-satan`)

Cited ayat: 59:15-17

> **59:15** كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ قَرِيبًا ذَاقُوا۟ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
>
> **59:16** كَمَثَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِذْ قَالَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ ٱكْفُرْ فَلَمَّا كَفَرَ قَالَ إِنِّى بَرِىٓءٌ مِّنكَ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
>
> **59:17** فَكَانَ عَٰقِبَتَهُمَآ أَنَّهُمَا فِى ٱلنَّارِ خَٰلِدَيْنِ فِيهَا وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (59:15): They are like those shortly before them who tasted the evil result of their conduct; for them is a painful punishment.

**c2** (59:16): They are like Satan when he said to the human being: disbelieve; then when he disbelieved, he said: I am free of you, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.

**c3** (59:17): The end of both is that they are in the Fire, abiding in it; that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.

### One-minute summary

The ayat compare them to those shortly before them who tasted the evil result of their conduct, and to Satan, who said to the human being: disbelieve [c1][c2]. The end of both is the Fire, which is the recompense of the wrongdoers [c3].

### Complete story

They are like those shortly before them who tasted the evil result of their conduct; for them is a painful punishment [c1].

They are like Satan when he said to the human being: disbelieve; then when he disbelieved, he said: I am free of you, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds [c2]. The end of both is that they are in the Fire, abiding in it; that is the recompense of the wrongdoers [c3].

### Deep study

The ayat give comparisons, one with people shortly before them and one with Satan, and draw one ending for both [c1][c2][c3]. The words of Satan are recorded in stages: his saying disbelieve and then his saying that he is free of the one who disbelieved [c2].

### Kids mode

The ayat say that Satan told a human being to disbelieve, and then said he was free of him [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show Satan's words changing once the human being obeyed [c2]. Another is that the ayat describe the end of the wrongdoers as the Fire [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who those shortly before them were, or what they did; the ayah says they tasted the evil result of their conduct.
- Not established: which human being is meant in the comparison with Satan; the ayah speaks of the human being in general.
- Not established: when or where the words of Satan were spoken.
- The ayat do not say how this comparison is tied to the particular events of the expulsion.
